samples.text: I have been meaning to write to you properly for some weeks now, and I keep putting it off because every time I sit down to do it I find that what I actually want to say is more complicated than the version I had rehearsed on the walk home; so forgive me if this wanders a little before it arrives anywhere.

My father handled all of the money when I was growing up, which meant that the rest of us learned about our circumstances indirectly, through his moods and through what quietly stopped appearing in the house, and I think that is a large part of why I still find it so difficult to raise the subject first, even with someone I trust as much as I trust Ana.

I would say that security matters more to me than almost anything else, although I am aware as I write it that I have not always behaved as though honesty mattered equally, and the bicycle is the obvious example of that, since I hid it for six weeks while telling myself that I was simply waiting for the right moment.
